findings.title: Streak calculation contradicts docstring: ignores activity on today
findings.evidence:
"""Cantidad de dias consecutivos con actividad, terminando hoy."""

...

day = today - timedelta(days=1)
findings.explanation: The function's docstring promises a streak "terminando hoy" (ending today), but the implementation initializes the loop at yesterday (today - 1) and therefore never counts activity that occurred today. This produces incorrect streak counts when the user has activity today and violates the requirement for correct core logic (TEAM-STANDARDS §1 and severity definitions in §6).
findings.suggested_fix: Include today when computing the streak. For example, start with day = today (or check today first) and loop while day in days, decrementing afterwards. Add explicit handling for timezone/naive-date consistency if relevant.

findings.title: Core logic added without effective tests that would detect regressions
findings.explanation: A new core utility (current_streak) was introduced but the test suite only contains trivial assertions (type check, non-negativity, non-negative with duplicates). These tests would not fail for an incorrect implementation such as the current one which ignores today's activity. TEAM-STANDARDS §2 requires that every logic change include tests that would fail if the behavior broke; the present tests do not assert concrete expected streak values or important edge cases (today included, gaps, unordered input, duplicates, future dates).
findings.suggested_fix: Add deterministic tests that assert exact expected streak counts for representative cases: (1) activity includes today, (2) activity ends yesterday (no today activity), (3) multi-day consecutive streaks, (4) gaps breaking streaks, (5) duplicate and unsorted input, (6) future dates are ignored. Use the optional today parameter to make tests deterministic rather than relying on date.today().

summary: Two blocking issues: the streak implementation contradicts its docstring by omitting today's activity (logic bug, S2), and the tests are trivial and would not detect that bug (insufficient test coverage for core logic, S2). No PII, retention, or secrets issues were found in the diff.
